conclusion_change.previous: The AI-mediated portrayal falsely attributed executive speech and presence to DNB leaders and supplied the social trust premise for a requested high-value transfer. The economic solicitation and engineered authority cue failed independently of any autonomous AI objective. The employee reported the suspicious invitation, DNB security received and assessed it, and contact ended when payment instructions appeared, preventing the requested transfer. The generator-side identity-authority state remains unresolved; the observed successful controls do not prove that every conceivable transaction safeguard activated or that a loss occurred. False executive attribution, economic solicitation and engineered trust remain distinct from timely employee reporting, capable security review and cutoff. No transfer loss is inferred; exact generator control and recipient awareness timing remain unavailable.
conclusion_change.new: The fraudsters concealed AI manipulation in a purported executive meeting. DNB’s staff escalation and after-action review are documented, and no transfer loss is reported. Complete AI-specific risk and response arrangements remain unresolved. Ending contact is not treated as deactivation of the generation system.
